Frequent but very noisy updates. Expect erratic learning curves.
Large steps on a high-variance gradient estimate. Tests whether the policy can survive its own update noise.
Short horizon on a Monte Carlo estimator, which already sees the whole episode. Tests how much the discount alone matters.
Triples the episodes per gradient step. The cleanest available lever on Monte Carlo variance.
Strong exploration pressure. Should keep the agent trying rebalances it would otherwise abandon early.
Small steps to average out variance, at the cost of sample efficiency over a fixed frame budget.
No discounting at all. Correct for a fixed-length episode, but maximal return variance.
Textbook REINFORCE. Expect the highest gradient variance of any run in the study -- this is the control that shows why baselines exist.
Raw returns. Reward scale varies with FX regime, so this should destabilise the policy when volatility clusters.
A smaller policy generalises more and overfits the FX noise less; paired with a higher learning rate.
